verses.text: These are the journeys of the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.

xrefs.text: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses before you, as well as Aaron and Miriam.
When Jacob went to Egypt, your fathers cried out to the LORD, and He sent them Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I afflicted the Egyptians by what I did there, and afterward I brought you out.
So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.

verses.text: At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey. These are the stages listed by their starting points:

xrefs.text: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out, and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of Mount Seir.
When you sound the short blasts a second time, the camps that lie on the south side are to set out. The blasts are to signal them to set out.
Then the LORD said to me, “Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people, that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.”
They set out this first time according to the LORD’s command through Moses.

verses.text: On the fifteenth day of the first month, on the day after the Passover, the Israelites set out from Rameses. They marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians,

xrefs.text: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out defiantly.
The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.
Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.
For you will not leave in a hurry nor flee in haste, for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard.
One who breaks open the way will go up before them; they will break through the gate, and go out by it. Their King will pass through before them, the LORD as their leader.

verses.text: who were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them; for the LORD had executed judgment against their gods.

xrefs.text: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
This is the burden against Egypt: Behold, the LORD rides on a swift cloud; He is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble before Him, and the hearts of the Egyptians will melt within them.
The LORD will be terrifying to them when He starves all the gods of the earth. Then the nations of every shore will bow in worship to Him, each in its own place.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for He did this when they treated Israel with arrogance.”
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.

verses.text: The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

xrefs.text: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.

verses.text: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

xrefs.text: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.

verses.text: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol.

xrefs.text: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. You are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon.
The Egyptians— all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, horsemen and troops— pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea, into the wilderness, and they journeyed three days into the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.

verses.text: They set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea, into the wilderness, and they journeyed three days into the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.

xrefs.text: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Desert of Shur. For three days they walked in the desert without finding water.

verses.text: They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

xrefs.text: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.

verses.text: They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.

xrefs.text: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.

verses.text: They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the Desert of Sin.

verses.text: They set out from Rephidim and camped in the Wilderness of Sinai.

xrefs.text: In the third month, on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.
On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.

xrefs.text: So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.

The LORD our God said to us at Horeb: “You have stayed at this mountain long enough.
So they set out on a three-day journey from the mountain of the LORD, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD traveling ahead of them for those three days to seek a resting place for them.

verses.text: They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

xrefs.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.

verses.text: They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

xrefs.text: After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.

verses.text: They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.

xrefs.text: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan— in the Arabah opposite Suph— between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.

They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.

They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.

xrefs.text: and I went back down the mountain and placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me; and there they have remained.

verses.text: They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.

xrefs.text: The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son succeeded him as priest.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites: Bela son of Beor. His city was named Dinhabah.
These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

verses.text: They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.

xrefs.text: From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.

verses.text: They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.

xrefs.text: From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.

verses.text: They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.

xrefs.text: So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We turned away from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber, and traveled along the road of the Wilderness of Moab.
King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.
Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they never set sail, because they were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
They agreed to make ships to go to Tarshish, and these were built in Ezion-geber.
Now since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.

verses.text: They set out from Ezion-geber and camped at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.

xrefs.text: In the first month, the whole congregation of Israel entered the Wilderness of Zin and stayed in Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.

for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin.
For at the waters of Meribah-kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you broke faith with Me among the Israelites by failing to treat Me as holy in their presence.
So they went up and spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.

verses.text: They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the outskirts of the land of Edom.

and when we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Now look, we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.

verses.text: At the LORD’s command, Aaron the priest climbed Mount Hor and died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt.

xrefs.text: The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son succeeded him as priest.

“Aaron will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.

verses.text: Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
Now the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.

xrefs.text: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.

verses.text: And the Israelites set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.

xrefs.text: Then the Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.

verses.text: They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim on the border of Moab.

xrefs.text: They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab to the east.

verses.text: They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.

Dibon goes up to its temple to weep at its high places. Moab wails over Nebo, as well as over Medeba. Every head is shaved, every beard is cut off.
Come down from your glory; sit on parched ground, O daughter dwelling in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.
I will stretch out My hand against them, and wherever they live I will make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”

verses.text: They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim facing Nebo.

and from Bamoth to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland.

While Israel was staying in Shittim, the men began to indulge in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab,
therefore I will indeed expose the flank of Moab beginning with its frontier cities— Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim— the glory of the land.

verses.text: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

xrefs.text: The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over the dry ground, until the entire nation had crossed the Jordan.
Hear, O Israel: Today you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, with large cities fortified to the heavens.

When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, and He drives out before you many nations— the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations larger and stronger than you—

verses.text: you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land, destroy all their carved images and cast idols, and demolish all their high places.

xrefs.text: [“]You must not make idols for yourselves or set up a carved image or sacred pillar; you must not place a sculpted stone in your land to bow down to it. For I am the LORD your God.
You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
However, in the cities of the nations that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
and when the LORD your God has delivered them over to you to defeat them, then you must devote them to complete destruction. Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.
Destroy completely all the places where the nations you are dispossessing have served their gods— atop the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.

verses.text: You are to take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.

xrefs.text: For you are about to cross the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. When you take possession of it and settle in it,

You will be driven away from mankind to live with the beasts of the field, and you will feed on grass like an ox. And seven times will pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.”
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when He divided the sons of man, He set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God.
Thus the LORD gave Israel all the land He had sworn to give their fathers, and they took possession of it and settled in it.
The highest heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to mankind.

verses.text: And you are to divide the land by lot according to your clans. Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one. Whatever falls to each one by lot will be his. You will receive an inheritance according to the tribes of your fathers.

xrefs.text: “The land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
Now the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah extended to the border of Edom, to the Wilderness of Zin at the extreme southern boundary:
The allotment for the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho on the east, through the wilderness that goes up from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.

Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh as Joseph’s firstborn son, namely for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh and father of the Gileadites, who had received Gilead and Bashan because Machir was a man of war.
The first lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Benjamin. Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Judah and Joseph:

verses.text: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, those you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides; they will harass you in the land where you settle.

xrefs.text: So now I tell you that I will not drive out these people before you; they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.”

because they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will swiftly destroy you.
